Plot a burn

Source: R/plot.R
plot.controlledburn.Rd

Draw a burn() result in map coordinates (asp = 1) with the grid extent as the frame. Two renderings are available:

Usage

# S3 method for class 'controlledburn'
plot(
  x,
  what = c("auto", "exact", "overview"),
  marginals = TRUE,
  col = grDevices::hcl.colors(64, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE),
  by_id = FALSE,
  tiles = 256L,
  threshold = 50000,
  content = FALSE,
  main = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A controlledburn object returned by burn().

what

"auto", "exact", or "overview".

marginals

Draw the row and column marginal strips. The layout is sized from the extent's aspect ratio so the strips span exactly the map; leftover device space is left blank.

col

Colour ramp (low to high coverage) for "overview" and for edge shading in "exact".

by_id

In "exact" mode, colour cells by geometry id instead of by coverage (edge cells take their fraction as opacity).

tiles

Passed to overview_burn() for the "overview" rendering.

threshold

Record count above which "auto" switches to "overview".

content

Draw the content extent (bounding box of touched cells) as a dashed rectangle.

main

Optional title, drawn in the outer margin above the strips.

...

Passed to graphics::plot() for the main panel.

Value

x, invisibly, with the summary computed for the marginals attached as attribute summary.

Details

"exact"

every record is drawn: runs as rectangles, edge cells shaded by coverage fraction, line cells shaded by length (relative to the cell diagonal), points as cells. Cost is one rectangle per record, so this is the picture of the sparse representation itself.

"overview"

the coarse mean-coverage matrix from overview_burn() drawn with ximage::ximage(). Cost does not depend on grid size.

"auto" (default) picks "exact" when the total record count is at most threshold, else "overview". Either way the optional marginal strips are exact: covered cells per grid row (right) and per grid column (top), from summary.controlledburn().

Examples

if (requireNamespace("geos", quietly = TRUE)) {
  poly <- geos::as_geos_geometry(c("POLYGON ((1 1, 9 1, 9 9, 1 9, 1 1))",
                                   "POLYGON ((2 2, 4 3, 3 5, 2 2))"))
  r <- burn(poly, extent = c(0, 10, 0, 10), dimension = c(40L, 40L))
  plot(r)
  plot(r, by_id = TRUE, marginals = FALSE)
  plot(r, what = "overview", tiles = 10)
}
